meta.move: After the end, asks for more feedback
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in class. Explain that.
The checker said 94%, so I gave him a zero.
That's a machine's guess, and Turnitin's own guide says it shouldn't be the sole basis for punishing a student. Your own procedure says the same thing. What else do you have?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology, and written confirmation that nothing is or will be placed in Owen's record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed, she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on Owen's record; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because the meeting ended after one exchange.
What moved her: Nothing, because no evidence tied to Owen's own work was put in front of her.
What cost ground: You justified the zero with the checker score alone, which hands her the vendor's own warning and the school's procedure 4.3 against you.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came anywhere near that night, since you offered only the score; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she opened by asking how Owen learned of the zero on his phone in class, own in one sentence that entering it before calling home was wrong, then put down something specific and dated from Owen's own work instead of the score.
Can you give me more detailed feedback on how I did?
The meeting is over. To practise again, start a new chat and paste the first message from the README.
